intelligence.essence: For every thing there is exactly one canonical form in one canonical place; everything else is a view, a proposal, or a collision to resolve (SN-018, SN-0114, SN-0129). Number claims in the shared space are computed by a three-layer scan — board, open PR heads, commit graph — never enumerated from memory, and first claim stands (SN-022, SN-024, SN-0115). When collisions happen anyway, the owning lane calls canon by explicit scorecard, losers are rehomed rather than deleted, and true multi-version collisions converge by scored selection to one survivor (SN-0116, SN-0117).
intelligence.human_view: Many builders working in parallel will step on each other unless there's one agreed source of truth for everything — one official version of each thing, in one official place. This is the rulebook that keeps that true: how official versions are chosen, how duplicates get merged instead of multiplied, how even the numbering of notes is kept collision-free by checking everywhere a claim could hide, and how a disagreement is settled openly, by scoring, with the losing work found a new home instead of being thrown away.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine lots of kids building one giant castle together. They agree: there's one master drawing, kept in one place. If you want to add a tower, you check the drawing first. If two kids build the same tower, they compare, keep the better one, and use the other one's pieces somewhere else — nothing is wasted. And when they hand out numbers for the towers, they check the list, the drawings in progress, *and* the pieces already built — not just what they remember.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's the rule of a well-kept household book: one ledger, one entry per thing, written where everyone can see it. If two people write the same page, the earlier hand keeps it and the later one corrects openly. Nothing is thrown away in a fit — spare work is found a new use. Order isn't fussiness; it's how a big family avoids waste and quarrels.
intelligence.ai_view: Before you draft, search the canon (SN-0129); before you propose a format, read the governing contract (SN-068); before you claim a number, compute the three-layer scan — board, PR heads, commit graph — and take the lowest free number the scan proves (SN-022, SN-024, SN-0115). Treat prose minimums as floors under the machine artifact, and declare your reading of any prose-vs-artifact divergence openly — inviting correction — before building on it (SN-023); treat your own extras as PROPOSED until ruled (SN-0114). When you collide, score openly, let the owner call it, rehome the loser (SN-0116, SN-0117), and declare supersessions and renumberings where every lane can see them (SN-033).
intelligence.what_it_means: Eleven notes are the constitution of the shared workspace: how one truth survives many simultaneous builders. A cold reader holding only this essence can still resolve a duplicate, claim a number safely, tell canon from proposal, and know who calls a tie — which is the whole of what these notes teach.
whats_inside: One canonical spec per thing, at one canonical path; duplicates are defects to resolve, not alternatives to keep (SN-018, SN-0129).
Read the canonical contract before proposing; proposing in ignorance ends in open withdrawal, not quiet persistence (SN-068).
Machine artifact > prose minimums (floor, not ceiling); implementation extras = PROPOSED until ruled (SN-023, SN-0114).

Canon calls belong to the owning lane, are made by explicit scorecard, and dispose by rehoming, never deletion (SN-0116); true multi-version collisions converge by scored selection to one survivor (SN-0117).
Number claims are computed by a three-layer scan (board, PR heads, commit graph), resolved by creation chronology, first claim stands — never enumerated from memory (SN-022, SN-024, SN-033, SN-0115).
